title: Note with a Quote

illustrates.quote: Notes Containing Displayed Quoted Material. When a note contains quoted matter set off from the body of the note by blank lines, quotation marks, change of margins, or font attributes, use the listed format of 1-3 for the note, and use the guidelines found in Formats, §9, Displayed Material, Attributions, and Source Information. (See Sample 16-5: Note with a Quote on page 16-22.)

blocks.text: 'Sheridan will not succeed at Bath with his oratory. Ridicule has gone down before him, and, I doubt, Derrick is his enemy.'[ref:*]
blocks.features: Single quoted sentence with an asterisk reference mark at the end.

blocks.text:
*Mr. Sheridan was then reading lectures upon Oratory at Bath, where Derrick was Master of the Ceremonies; or, as the phrase is, KING BOSWELL. Dr. Parr, who knew Sheridan well, describes him 'as a wrong-headed, whimsical man.' …Take a sample:
“None but the brave
None but the brave.
None but the brave deserve the fair.”
Naughty Richard [R. B. Sheridan], like Gallio, seemed to care nought for these things.' Moore's Sheridan, i. 9, 11.
blocks.features: Long footnote containing, part-way through, a three-line displayed poem quotation set off by its own blank lines and centered layout, followed by a closing attribution.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.7.4 per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: lines 12988(sic)/13014/13018/13023/13027/13029/13030 area (field width 5, digits(19)+3) reach exactly 40 characters on several lines; line 13013 (41 characters) is a genuine one-cell source anomaly, flagged in uncertain, not a transcription slip -- both runs already agree on this line's content. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
